answer: Withdrawal rights live in a vault that opens only along a thread of settled history. A new identity starts with a zero-length thread, so its outflow cap is near nothing; each settlement with a distinct counterparty lengthens the thread and raises the cap, while repeat counterparties add nothing. Reaching the summit tier unlocks transfers, and splicing two threads yields the longer one, never the sum, so pooling cannot manufacture capacity. The k-th splice burns k times the base bond, so n fakes with usable threads cost a staircase near n squared, and each still needs a genuine counterparty.
